title: Armenian parliament passes a bill launching the process of joining the European Union
body:
On 26 March 2025 Armenia's parliament approved, in its second and final reading, a bill calling on the government to begin the process of joining the European Union. The vote was 64 in favour, all from the ruling Civil Contract party, and 7 against, all from opposition lawmakers. Artak Zeynalian, a former justice minister representing a group that backs EU membership, said the process was irreversible. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan had backed the bill in January but said EU membership would require a referendum and major reforms, including in the justice system.

Russia reacted strongly. Deputy Prime Minister Aleksei Overchuk said in January that starting EU accession meant leaving the Eurasian Economic Union, and Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu warned that Armenia could lose tariff-free trade with Russia, face higher gas prices and see large numbers of Armenian migrant workers expelled.

RFE/RL placed the vote against a background of frayed relations with Moscow, which Yerevan accused of doing nothing to stop Azerbaijan's September 2023 takeover of Nagorno-Karabakh, after which nearly 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled. Armenia had frozen its CSTO participation in February 2024, joined the International Criminal Court, held drills with US troops in June 2024 and signed a strategic partnership with the United States in January 2025.
